stories.delivered_paragraph: India has introduced legislation that could let merchants be charged for some Unified Payments Interface transactions, challenging the zero-fee regime that has applied since 2020. UPI processed a record 23.66 billion payments worth ₹29.88 trillion, about $313.4 billion, in July, while banks and fintechs argue state incentives are no longer enough to fund the network. The bill opens a politically sensitive debate over how to sustain a payment system used across the economy.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Trump Media & Technology Group has launched Truth API, a paid data feed promising Wall Street firms and institutional investors the fastest access to influential Truth Social posts. The offering raises ethical and legal questions because President Donald Trump’s account, with about 13 million followers, can move markets and his family remains the company’s majority shareholder. The service could intensify scrutiny over whether privileged speed in receiving presidential statements should be sold commercially.

stories.delivered_paragraph: AI infrastructure company Runware has launched the Sonic Inference Pod, a transportable modular data center designed to add computing capacity wherever power is available. The company says its closed-loop cooling system uses no water and can be built in days rather than the months or years needed for conventional facilities. Runware is betting that distributed compute placed closer to users will lower costs and speed AI responses as demand for inference grows.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Pfizer beat quarterly estimates and raised the lower end of its full-year revenue outlook, citing strength in Eliquis and other medicines, but cut its expected 2026 revenue from Covid products to $4 billion from roughly $5 billion. The revision underscores how sharply the pandemic business is fading even as the drugmaker’s established portfolio supports its broader forecast. Investors will be watching whether newer products can further offset lost Covid sales.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Prediction-market operator Polymarket is reportedly in talks to raise funding at a valuation above $20 billion, following rapid growth in trading tied to politics, economics and other real-world events. The company told CNBC in June that its annualized revenue had risen above $1 billion. A deal at that price would mark a major vote of confidence in event-contract markets, while putting more focus on their regulatory treatment and ability to sustain activity beyond major news cycles.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Cameroon’s 93-year-old President Paul Biya reshuffled senior military posts after being absent from public view for nearly two months, promoting five colonels to brigadier general. He reappointed Raymond Jean Charles Beko’o Abondo to command the elite presidential guard, a job he has held since 2013. Although such shake-ups are common under Biya, the timing is fueling concern about stability and succession around the world’s oldest serving president.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ukrainian drone strikes hit two Wildberries sites in Russia and damaged another industrial location near Moscow, where local officials said five people were killed and 10 injured. Russia’s strikes across Ukraine killed at least four people, showing both sides continue to target infrastructure as the war’s aerial campaign expands.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Guatemala’s Fuego volcano erupted, sending lava into the air from one of Central America’s most active volcanoes. The event highlights the recurring hazard faced by communities and travelers around Fuego, where activity can change quickly.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The San Sebastián Film Festival will stage a 20-film retrospective of José Giovanni, the French writer-director whose work helped define postwar crime cinema. The program at the festival’s 74th edition spans films released from 1960 to 2001, including nearly all his directing work and eight screenplays for other filmmakers. It will revisit a career shaped by Giovanni’s own imprisonment and death sentence, which was later commuted to hard labor.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said the central bank’s 3.5%-3.75% benchmark rate is sufficiently restrictive for now to return inflation to its 2% goal, though she remains open-minded about later changes. Her comments reinforce the Fed’s cautious stance as officials seek clearer evidence that inflation is easing.

stories.delivered_paragraph: US stock futures rose Tuesday as oil prices fell on reports of possible US-Iran talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while strong results from Palantir and Caterpillar added support. stories.delivered_paragraph: Palantir shares jumped about 20% after the software company reported second-quarter revenue up 93% from a year earlier to $1.94 billion, ahead of the $1.8 billion expected by analysts. Commercial revenue rose 149% to $764 million as customers sought AI tools that keep their data under their own control, while government revenue grew 90%. The results strengthen Palantir’s case that demand for enterprise and sovereign AI is becoming a meaningful growth engine.
